newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Swedish debt yields ended Monday's session mixed with T-bill rates slightly lower and bond yields pushed higher by rising foreign debt yields.
Finland's decision to link the markka to ERM had little impact on the Swedish debt market.
"The Finnish move was widely expected, and the Swedish stance that an ERM link is not at the agenda is also well known," said one dealer.
Six-month T-bill rates closed two basis points lower at 4.61 percent and nine-year bond yields rose four basis points to 7.18 percent.
The crown managed to firm slightly to 4.2950 against the mark from 4.3100 crowns late Friday.

Dealers were now focusing on Tuesday's weekly Riksbank repo operation. A Reuter survey showed nine of eleven economists and analysts expecting the repo rate to be unchanged but two forecast the central bank would break its pattern of bi-weekly ten basis point cuts and trim again.
The repo rate, the riksbank's key tool for controlling money market liquidity, was last eased by 10 basis point to 4.95 percent last Tuesday.
